findings.diagnosis: The scorer habitually prefers cutting after content heads instead of moving the cut left to leave a non-assertive / functional prefix; that choice produces fragments that assert misleading facts when the later piece arrives.
findings.evidence: 9 cases (en_us_888, en_us_767, en_us_1488, en_us_1253, en_us_741, en_us_419, en_us_924, en_us_1615, en_us_1199). In each, the offline target moves the cut earlier (often to a determiner/pronoun/auxiliary), making the preceding fragment inert and raising H_set.
